re_line: Australia-Solomon Islands treaty bars foreign bases · Honiara lets 2022 China pact lapse in April · Inflation hits 4.9%, three-year high · Digital Duty of Care passes with 5% revenue fines · Victorian election Saturday
morning_memo: Solomon Islands signed a sweeping security treaty with Australia barring foreign military bases from its territory, after quietly telling Beijing it will let its 2022 police pact lapse when it comes up for renewal next April.
French forces seized more than 3.3 tonnes of methamphetamine from an unflagged tanker near French Polynesia, in an operation supported by a US Coast Guard maritime patrol aircraft.
Australian headline inflation jumped to 4.9 percent in October, the highest in three years, sharpening a stagflation debate that is testing Treasurer Jim Chalmers in the final sitting week of 2026.

top_stories.headline: Australia and Solomon Islands sign treaty barring foreign military bases
top_stories.body: Australia and Solomon Islands signed a treaty in Canberra barring any foreign military or security base from Solomon Islands territory and committing Honiara to keep sensitive infrastructure free from militarisation, foreign interference and unauthorised access. Prime Ministers **Anthony Albanese** and **Matthew Wale** signed after Wale led a *twenty-four-member delegation*, including fifteen ministers, to the capital. The ABC reported Wale's government has told Beijing it will let the 2022 security pact, which allowed rotating Chinese police trainers, phase out at renewal in April.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH (Matthew Knott): "'Hard to overstate': Australia celebrates diplomatic coup, locks out China in Solomons pact" · also New York Times, AP, RNZ Pacific

top_stories.headline: Inflation hits three-year high, stagflation fears grip Canberra
top_stories.body: Australian headline inflation reached *4.9 percent* in the twelve months to October, the highest in three years and up from 4.3 percent in September. Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** called the figure unwelcome but expected, citing global pressures, and pushed back on the word stagflation. Reserve Bank research released alongside the data found even households untouched by rate rises are cutting back on essentials. Shadow Treasurer **Tim Wilson** said government spending was solely to blame.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH: "Stagflation fears grip Canberra as inflation, unemployment surge" · also ABC News, Wall Street Journal

top_stories.headline: Digital Duty of Care law clears parliament, Big Tech faces billions in fines
top_stories.body: Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Bill after Labor struck a deal with the Greens, exposing technology platforms to fines of up to *5 percent* of global revenue for failing to prevent online harms. The Coalition opposed it, making this the first Australian online safety law to pass without bipartisan support. Shadow minister for industry **Andrew Hastie** called the legislation "heavy-handed censorship" and raised free speech concerns.
top_stories.src_line: per AP: "Australia passes online safety law, putting Big Tech at risk of multibillion-dollar fines" · also Washington Post

overnight_items.headline: French forces seize 3.3 tonnes of meth from unflagged tanker near French Polynesia
overnight_items.body_text: The French Pacific Command and French Armed Forces in Asia-Pacific and French Polynesia seized *more than 3.3 tonnes* of methamphetamine from an unflagged light oil tanker outside French Polynesia's maritime zone last Friday. Fusion centres in French Polynesia and New Caledonia had tracked the vessel for weeks with international partners; a US Coast Guard maritime patrol aircraft supported the boarding. The 150 barrels were taken to Tahiti for destruction and the crew released after an international report was filed.

overnight_items.headline: Beijing says it does not engage in 'geopolitical manoeuvring' after Solomons decision
overnight_items.body_text: A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman responded to reports Solomon Islands will not renew its 2022 security pact by saying China does not engage in geopolitical manoeuvring or target any third party in its cooperation with Pacific Island nations. ABC foreign affairs reporter **Stephen Dziedzic** said the agreement does not lapse immediately: Honiara has signalled it will not proceed when renewal falls due in about April.

overnight_items.headline: Report flags gaps in Australia's grasp of critical infrastructure risk
overnight_items.body_text: The Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering said Australia must recognise digital and AI infrastructure as critical, echoing warnings in **Penny Wong**'s foreign policy address to parliament. Wong said artificial intelligence is "reshaping the foundations of our societies" and that trade settings, investment flows, shipping lanes, food security, undersea cables and critical minerals are all being weaponised.

overnight_items.headline: US Army auditors warn key units unprepared for a Pacific war scenario
overnight_items.body_text: A PACNEWS bulletin reports US Army auditors fear key units are unprepared to deploy in a Pacific war scenario. The same bulletin carries Vanuatu and US Coast Guard joint maritime patrols and an EU-funded programme reaching more than 513,000 people in Papua New Guinea's Sepik region.

overnight_items.headline: Forum Fisheries Agency rolls out PacGuard surveillance system
overnight_items.body_text: The Forum Fisheries Agency has launched PacGuard, an advanced maritime surveillance system for the Pacific, as fisheries officials prepare for the WCPFC23 negotiations on bigeye tuna catch limits and fishing rules. Vanuatu will host the meeting. Islands Business notes the Western and Central Pacific fishery yields about $3 billion in tuna catch a year, of which the Pacific receives 6.25 percent of the value.

overnight_items.headline: Kiwi slides as New Zealand's election count drags on
overnight_items.body_text: The New Zealand dollar is falling as the post-election count continues without a resolution, The Australian reported, comparing the kiwi's slide unfavourably with the Australian dollar's own weakness. The NZD/USD stood at 0.5461, down 0.51 percent, and the NZX 50 at 14,048, down 1.32 percent.

aukus_watch.headline: ASPI urges Defence to turn Australia's quantum edge into a deterrent
aukus_watch.body_text: Defence should establish a procurement-to-export programme for quantum clocks and sensors that connects successful trials to military qualification, Australian production and allied orders, ASPI argues. Integrating the Australian Defence Force throughout development would help embed the emerging technologies in force structure.

aukus_watch.headline: ASPI: Australia and Japan should build a joint missile maintenance facility
aukus_watch.body_text: Japan and Australia should establish a joint facility in Australia for maintaining missiles, strengthening their ability to sustain military operations and reinforcing deterrence against China, ASPI argues. The authors say the facility would also deliver on US objectives for allied sustainment capacity.

aukus_watch.headline: Independent MP calls new defence legislation 'very rushed and an overreach'
aukus_watch.body_text: An independent MP told ABC Radio National Breakfast that Canberra's new defence legislation is "very rushed and an overreach." The bill follows reporting on November 19 that Australia would set a seven-year prison term for photographing defence sites.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG government vows 'full force of the law' after five women buried alive
pacific_wire.body_text: Five women, one of them pregnant, were allegedly buried alive in Kaa village, Southern Highlands Province, over sorcery accusations. Police Commissioner **David Manning** confirmed three men are in custody. Police Minister **John Pundari** said those responsible, and those who failed to prevent the offending, would be held to account.

pacific_wire.headline: Juffa urges PNG parliament to formally accept Bougainville referendum result
pacific_wire.body_text: Oro Governor **Garry Juffa** told parliament to cut through confusion on the floor and vote to formally accept the 2019 Bougainville referendum results, warning MPs to guard against foreign interests afterwards. Prime Minister **James Marape** thanked Bougainville's leaders and people for respecting the parliamentary process during the debate.

pacific_wire.headline: US Coast Guard cutter returns to Vanuatu for joint patrols
pacific_wire.body_text: The US Coast Guard Cutter Harriet Lane has returned to Vanuatu for joint maritime law enforcement operations with Vanuatu officials under the 2016 US-Vanuatu Bilateral Maritime Law Enforcement Agreement, the US Embassy in Port Vila said.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji launches first national fisheries transparency workshop
pacific_wire.body_text: Minister for Fisheries and Forestry **Alitia Bainivalu** opened Fiji's first national Fisheries Transparency Initiative workshop in Suva, flagging public access to fisheries data across the country's 1.29 million square kilometre ocean territory. Fiji became the first Pacific island nation to join FiTI after signing a memorandum with executive director **Sven Biermann** in Rome.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji elections office prepares for a possible simultaneous referendum
pacific_wire.body_text: The Fijian Elections Office is preparing for the 2026 general election while making provisions for a national referendum on the same day. Supervisor of Elections **Ana Mataiciwa** said running two electoral events simultaneously would require additional processes and logistical arrangements.

pacific_wire.headline: UNAIDS: new Pacific HIV infections up 65 percent since 2010
pacific_wire.body_text: New HIV infections across the Pacific rose an estimated *65 percent* and AIDS-related deaths 19 percent between 2010 and 2025, against declines of 21 and 59 percent across Asia and the Pacific overall. Papua New Guinea has the largest epidemic, with 110,000 people living with HIV. Fiji's new infections have risen twelve-fold since 2010, reaching 1,700 in 2025. UNAIDS flagged increases in Palau, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu.

pacific_wire.headline: Kamikamica warns pilot insurance schemes are not yet markets
pacific_wire.body_text: Deputy Prime Minister **Manoa Kamikamica** opened the Pacific Regional Workshop on Climate and Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance in Suva, noting losses after Tropical Cyclone Winston in 2016 equalled roughly a third of Fiji's national income. He launched SmartPak for micro, small and medium enterprises, which contribute about 18 percent of GDP, and cautioned that "a pilot proves something can work, but it does not prove that the market will last."

new_zealand.headline: Wellington watches as Canberra locks in Solomon Islands security role
new_zealand.body_text: New Zealand's 1News reported the Australia-Solomon Islands treaty as a potentially significant reconfiguration of the order of influence in the region, following Honiara's decision to scrap its pact with China. The treaty makes Australia Solomon Islands' primary security partner.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealand retains Serco naval training contract
new_zealand.body_text: New Zealand has retained Serco on its naval training contract, Australian Defence Magazine reported. The decision keeps an incumbent provider in place for Royal New Zealand Navy training as the incoming government's defence settings remain unresolved pending the election count.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Analysts weigh what Solomon Islanders get from the Australian treaty
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: The new treaty tears up a previous deal between Solomon Islands and China, but carries substantial domestic content for Solomon Islanders, The Conversation argues. Canberra will help strengthen the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force, support the government's free education policy, and open aged care and childcare work opportunities in Australia.

canberra_politics.headline: Essential poll: Albanese's disapproval hits its highest recorded level
canberra_politics.body_text: **Anthony Albanese**'s net popularity fell 10 points in a month in the latest Guardian Essential poll, taking his disapproval to its highest recorded level. Nearly half of respondents said they do not want an AI data centre near their home, with women, older voters, and One Nation and Greens supporters most opposed.

canberra_politics.headline: Capital gains carve-out for businesses heads to a Senate inquiry
canberra_politics.body_text: Independent MP **Allegra Spender**'s proposal to apply a flat 40 percent capital gains discount to all active business assets is headed for a Senate inquiry, pushing the matter into next year. **Jim Chalmers** wrote to Spender last week saying her idea would not be "simpler, fairer, or enhance productivity," and Treasury has warned it is complex and could be gamed.

canberra_politics.headline: Bowen says the words 'fossil fuels' derailed COP31
canberra_politics.body_text: Climate Change and Energy Minister **Chris Bowen**, in his first interview since the summit, said negotiations "were going quite well, then got caught up in the use of the words 'fossil fuels.'" The talks in Türkiye, co-led by Australia, collapsed on Sunday after several countries and the EU rejected a text omitting the phrase. Opposition Leader **Angus Taylor** has called for Bowen to resign.

canberra_politics.headline: Greens deal delivers Labor a minimum 30 percent tax on trust distributions
canberra_politics.body_text: Labor struck a deal with the Greens to impose a minimum *30 percent* tax on distributions from discretionary trusts. The Greens dropped a demand to apply the tax to payments made to private schools and charities; Senator **Nick McKim** said the party instead secured an increase in the tax on jet fuel for private plane owners.

canberra_politics.headline: Australia formally apologises to LGBTQ veterans
canberra_politics.body_text: Thirty-four years after the Keating government overturned the ban on same-sex attracted people serving in the Australian Defence Force, the nation formally apologised. Albanese called the historic bans "a tragedy in the life of our nation."

canberra_politics.headline: Victorian polling points to a wipe-out of the 12-year-old Labor government
canberra_politics.body_text: Polling ahead of Saturday's Victorian state election points to a defeat for Labor, with pundits tipping a Liberal-National majority under **Jess Wilson**. Support for Labor among women sits at *16 percent*. Unions have pulled campaign funds, with Luke Hilakari accusing Deputy Premier Ben Carroll of leaving workers "on the porch."

business_economy.headline: RBA economists find mortgage holders three times as likely to use debt for essentials
business_economy.body_text: Households with mortgages are three times as likely to rely on debt and credit cards for daily essentials as the cash rate hits 4.85 per cent, RBA economists found. The AFR reported borrowers are also working longer hours to absorb repayments.

business_economy.headline: Harvey Norman pre-tax profit falls 47 percent as Gerry Harvey warns on recession
business_economy.body_text: **Gerry Harvey** said a recession "has to happen" as Harvey Norman pre-tax profits fell *47 percent* and the retailer cut supplier orders. The warning lands the same day headline inflation reached a three-year high.

business_economy.headline: US court convicts Huawei over Iran dealings and trade secret theft
business_economy.body_text: A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei of deceiving banks about its business in Iran and stealing trade secrets from US companies, after a trial running more than two months and more than 60 prosecution witnesses. The US placed Huawei on a trade blacklist in 2019, a year after the case began.

primary_documents.headline: Joint statement on the signing of the Australia-Solomon Islands Treaty
primary_documents.body_text: Albanese and Wale said the treaty would make Australia, Solomon Islands and the region "safer and more prosperous," affirming Solomon Islands' sovereignty and its capacity to determine its own security needs and partnerships. The statement commits both governments to joint economic, development and security priorities, and includes substantial support for Solomon Islands' free education policy.
primary_documents.key_line: The Treaty includes substantial support towards the Solomon Islands Government's free education policy, so that every child can reach their potential.

primary_documents.headline: Wong doorstop at Parliament House
primary_documents.body_text: The Foreign Minister took questions at Parliament House on the day of the Solomon Islands treaty signing, a day after delivering her foreign policy address to parliament.

calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Polling points to the defeat of a 12-year-old Labor government in Australia's second-largest state, with federal implications for Labor's standing.

calendar_watch.event: WCPFC23 tuna commission meeting, hosted by Vanuatu
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Delegates will decide bigeye tuna catch limits and fishing rules governing a fishery worth about $3 billion a year to the Western and Central Pacific.

calendar_watch.event: Renewal date of the Solomon Islands-China security agreement
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Honiara has told Beijing it will not proceed with renewal, which would end the 2022 arrangement that allowed rotating Chinese police trainers.

calendar_watch.event: Senate inquiry into capital gains tax carve-outs reports
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The inquiry pushes Allegra Spender's active-asset proposal into next year and delays resolution of Labor's capital gains regime.

calendar_watch.event: El Niño conditions forecast to persist across the Pacific
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Fiji's drought emergency could stretch into 2027, with drought risk also flagged for Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands.

key_stat.label: Australian headline inflation, 12 months to October
key_stat.context: The highest rate in three years, up from 4.3 percent in September, with the RBA forecasting inflation outside its target band for another year.

also_today.headline: Devpolicy: locally led partnerships, not just assistive technology, drive Pacific disability outcomes
also_today.body_text: Pacific parents and service providers describe gaps in disability support systems, with the authors arguing locally led partnerships rather than technology transfer are the key to lasting change for children with disabilities.

also_today.headline: Lowy: collapsing language enrolments blunt Australia's ability to read a regional crisis
also_today.body_text: Falling Asian language enrolments have taken with them the capacity to read a regional crisis before it becomes one, the Interpreter argues, with implications for how Canberra anticipates disasters turning into security emergencies.

also_today.headline: Lowy: parliamentary report's conflict prevention tools only work as a system
also_today.body_text: A new parliamentary report's conflict prevention tools work only together, backed by early warning that tracks resilience as well as risk, the Interpreter argues.

also_today.headline: ASPI: northern Australia must prepare for overlapping major projects
also_today.body_text: After decades of worrying where the next major investment would come from, northern Australia's development advocates will increasingly need to plan for several arriving at once, with workforce and infrastructure sequencing the new constraint.

also_today.headline: Australian High Commissioner says Pacific climate commitment survives COP31
also_today.body_text: High Commissioner to Fiji **Peter Roberts** said Australia remains committed to amplifying Pacific voices despite the COP31 outcome, noting Canberra worked with Fiji and Tuvalu on the pre-COP meeting. He said Australia is exploring redirecting climate adaptation funds toward Fiji's immediate water shortages.

also_today.headline: Fiji's nationwide drought disaster exposes resilience gaps beyond sea level rise
also_today.body_text: Fiji's nationwide disaster declaration over El Niño drought exposes climate resilience challenges beyond the familiar threat of rising seas, The Diplomat reports. PACNEWS says the emergency could stretch into 2027.

opeds_today.headline: Is Albo terminal? No – but the world is in chaos and he will need to find his way through wicked problems
opeds_today.central_argument: Albanese ends the parliamentary year at his lowest ebb but retains room to rebuild public confidence.
opeds_today.summary: Lewis writes that the prime minister closes 2026 with global dysfunction lapping at Australia's shores, citing the collapse of the climate talks and the return of a compromised chief executive whose chips power the AI arms race. He argues the position is weak but not terminal.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Frames the domestic political constraint Albanese carries into 2027 even after a Pacific diplomatic win.
